title: Foreign Salary in NRE Account Not Taxable for NRIs: ITAT Clarifies
description: The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) Ahmedabad has ruled that foreign salary earned by an NRI outside India is not taxable in India. This non-taxable stat.

faq.q: Is all income earned by an NRI tax-free in India?
faq.a: No, only income earned outside India for services rendered outside India is generally tax-free for NRIs. Income that accrues or arises in India (e.g., rental income from Indian property, interest from NRO accounts, capital gains from Indian assets) is taxable in India.

faq.q: What if my foreign employer has an Indian entity and uses an Indian TAN for my salary?
faq.a: The ITAT ruling clarifies that the mere use of an Indian TAN or erroneous TDS deduction does not make foreign-sourced income taxable for an NRI. The key is where the services are rendered and your residential status.

faq.q: Can I transfer funds from my NRE account to an NRO account?
faq.a: Yes, you can transfer funds from an NRE account to an NRO (Non-Resident Ordinary) account. However, remember that interest earned on NRO accounts is taxable in India.

faq.q: What is the difference between an NRE and an NRO account?
faq.a: NRE accounts are for depositing foreign earnings, and both principal and interest are fully repatriable and interest is tax-exempt. NRO accounts are for managing Indian-sourced income (e.g., rent, dividends) and foreign income, but interest is taxable and only the current income (not principal) is generally repatriable after tax.

faq.q: Does this ruling apply to income other than salary?
faq.a: The specific ruling pertains to foreign salary. However, the underlying principle that foreign-sourced income of an NRI is not taxable in India generally extends to other forms of foreign income (e.g., foreign capital gains, foreign business income) as long as they are truly foreign-sourced and the individual maintains NR status.

faq.q: Where can I find official information on NRI taxation?
faq.a: You can find authoritative information on NRI taxation and residential status on the official Income Tax Department website.
